settings.heading: What the NHS and orthopaedic surgeons say about heat and massage
settings.intro: None of these people are selling anything. These are their words about warmth and massage on stiff joints in general, with the source linked so you can read it yourself.
settings.footnote: Jointwell is a comfort device. It is not a medical treatment and does not cure, treat or prevent any condition. Keep doing what your GP and physio have told you to do.

settings.role: nhs.uk, on easing joint stiffness at home
settings.quote: Heat applied to the affected area can be very effective in reducing pain.
Heat therapy is an easy, inexpensive, and medication-free way to relieve some types of arthritis stiffness and pain.

settings.role: Orthopaedic surgeon, hip and knee replacement
settings.quote: Using heat on sore or stiff joints can bring significant relief, especially when dealing with chronic arthritis pain.

settings.text: Heat-pack guidance says apply warmth for 15 to 20 minutes. A hot water bottle holds useful warmth for 20 to 30 minutes and a microwaved wheat bag about 30. The dose in your cupboard is roughly right. It is the delivery that runs out.
Knees, shoulders and elbows sit under thin skin with little muscle or fat around them, so they lose warmth faster than the rest of you and hold it worst. Cold hands, cold nose, cold knees.

NICE, which writes the guidance the NHS follows, puts exercise, weight management and information first for osteoarthritis. We are not a substitute for any of that. Warmth is what people use to get moving in the morning so they can do the rest.
settings.source: NICE guideline NG226, Osteoarthritis in over 16s (2022)

settings.title: Knee arthritis
settings.line: Wear and tear, the GP says. The first ten steps are the worst and the stairs are a decision.
settings.how: Straight round the knee, over or under trousers. The strap holds it while you walk to the kettle.
settings.when: First thing, with the first cup. Level 3, thirty minutes, before the stairs.
settings.note: Heat before you move, ice after a flare. That is what physios say, and it is all we say.
settings.alt: Woman at the kettle with the wrap on her knee

settings.title: Stiff shoulder
settings.line: The top shelf, the bra strap, sleeping on that side. Small things, twenty times a day.
settings.how: The extension strap in the box loops it over the shoulder and under the arm, so the warm panel sits on the joint.
settings.when: Under a cardigan while the tea brews, and again in the armchair in the evening.
settings.note: A wheat bag slides off a shoulder. This one stays.
settings.alt: Woman in an armchair with the wrap on her shoulder

settings.title: Tennis elbow
settings.line: From the secateurs and the watering can, not the tennis court. Worse when you grip.
settings.how: The strap takes it up the forearm to the elbow. Rest the arm on the chair and forget it.
settings.when: Before the garden, not after. Twenty to thirty minutes on the forearm as a warm-up.
settings.note: If the elbow is hot and sore to touch after a session, that is an ice day.
settings.alt: Woman doing a crossword with the wrap on her elbow

settings.title: After a knee replacement
settings.line: Ask your surgeon or physio first. Their word beats ours.
settings.how: Only once the wound has fully healed and they have said heat is fine. Start at the lowest level.
settings.when: The warm half hour before the exercise sheet, then the exercises.
settings.note: Never over a wound that has not healed, and never on a hot, red or newly swollen knee. That is a phone call to the clinic.
settings.alt: Woman at the breakfast table with the wrap on her knee

settings.title: Morning stiffness
settings.line: Hand on the wall, down the stairs sideways, fine by the afternoon. Then tomorrow.
settings.how: On the worst joint before you leave the kitchen. Kettle on, wrap on.
settings.when: Every morning for a month. Same chair, same cup. Habit is the whole trick.
settings.note: A joint that has not moved for eight hours is a cold joint. Warmth and movement are what wake it.
settings.alt: Woman by the window with the wrap on her knee

settings.title: Kneeling and gardening
settings.line: It is not the kneeling. It is getting down, and getting back up.
settings.how: Round the knee before the wellies go on. It is cordless, so it goes to the back door with you.
settings.when: Twenty minutes before you go out, and again in the chair when you come in.
settings.note: Two knees? Two wraps. The pair is the one most gardeners choose.
settings.alt: Woman on the carpet with the wrap on her knee

settings.title: Cold weather aches
settings.line: October to March. Some knees know the weather before the curtains are open.
settings.how: Under a dressing gown while the kettle boils, in the armchair with the television, in the car before a cold walk.
settings.when: Morning and evening on the coldest days. One charge covers the day for most people.
settings.note: One knee warm, not the whole house. The heating can stay where it is.

settings.question: Isn't this just a heating pad with extra steps?
settings.answer: A heating pad gives you heat that fades, or heat that ties you to a wall socket. Jointwell holds whichever of the five levels you pick, 45°C to 65°C, for a full 30 minutes. It adds vibration massage at three strengths, straps on so it stays put, and runs cordless in any chair in the house.

settings.question: Will it work for me? My joints have been like this a long time.
settings.answer: It isn't a cure and we won't pretend otherwise. Nobody can promise what it will do for your joint. What we can promise is warmth at the level you choose, held for thirty minutes, with massage alongside it. The 90-day trial is there so your own knee gets the deciding vote rather than our copy.

settings.question: Will it fit me?
settings.answer: One size, 46 cm across and 30 cm tall, with a 55 cm strap span. It fits either knee, and the extension strap in the box takes it round a shoulder or up an arm to the elbow. If it doesn't fit you, the 90-day trial covers a full refund and we pay the return postage.

settings.question: Is it safe? Will it burn me?
settings.answer: You choose the heat level, from a gentle 45°C up to 65°C, and every session shuts off after 30 minutes, so it cannot be left running. Do not use it while asleep. If you have diabetes, circulation problems or reduced skin sensation, check with your GP before using any heat product.

settings.question: When will it arrive?
settings.answer: We dispatch within 1 to 3 working days and most orders arrive within 7 to 10 working days of ordering, occasionally up to 14. Every order is tracked and we email you the link the moment it leaves us.

settings.question: How do I know this isn't another Facebook gadget?
settings.answer: Fair question, because this market is full of them. We dispatch most orders within 1 to 3 working days and track every one. There's a UK returns address, UK support, a 2-year warranty, and a 90-day trial where we pay the postage back. The reviews on this page are from customers with an order on file, in their own words. Junk sellers can't afford the guarantee.

settings.question: Can I use it after a knee replacement?
settings.answer: Ask your surgeon or physio first, and follow what they say. Many people are told heat is fine once the wound has fully healed, but that is their call, not ours. If they say yes, most people use it as the warm half hour before their exercises.

settings.question: How do I charge it, and how long does a charge last?
settings.answer: It charges over USB-C with the cable in the box, the same cable as most phones. It has a 3000 mAh battery. The panel shows the battery level.

settings.question: What happens if I send it back?
settings.answer: Email us within 90 days of delivery. We send you a UK returns address and a postage label. Post it back, and we refund what you paid in full once it arrives. You do not pay the postage and you do not have to give a reason, though we would like to hear it.

settings.question: Who shouldn't use it?
settings.answer: Anyone who has been told to avoid heat on that joint. If you have diabetes, circulation problems, reduced feeling in your skin, a pacemaker, an unhealed wound or a joint that is hot, red and swollen, talk to your GP before using any heat product. Do not use it while asleep, over broken skin, or on a child. If you are pregnant or under medical care for the joint, ask first. It is a comfort device, not a treatment, and your GP's word beats ours.
